note: What the cutter produced. One entry per raw sheet. `plate` marks a whole-frame layer copied as is (a backdrop, a tiling layer, a full-frame vignette, a shipped panel asset), with `plate_because` saying why. Otherwise the artwork was segmented from the sheet and every blob whose centre falls in a cell was gathered into that cell's sprite, so a shape drawn as several pieces stays one sprite. Each sprite is pasted centred on `canvas`: a sheet's sprites are all one size, and the `icons` family additionally shares a single 512px square canvas with every icon scaled to the same extent, while other families keep their own scale so a ship does not change size as it turns and a small asteroid stays small. `source_box` is where the artwork sat on the raw sheet. No keying, no alpha: the background is still in the file for the next pass.
